extracted.intended_audience: publishers (UK & Ireland) of literary fiction, commissioning editors, agents and authors entering the Man Booker Prize
extracted.subtask_description: Official rules and entry requirements for submitting novels to the 2018 Man Booker Prize, covering eligibility, publisher quotas, deadlines, required materials, and obligations if longlisted/shortlisted/winner.

rubrics_metrics.name: Awarding principle (judges' opinion)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Man Booker Prize is awarded annually by the Booker Prize Foundation to the author of the best (in the opinion of the judges) eligible novel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each year’s panel of judges is chosen with the advice of the Booker Prize Foundation Advisory Committee and is appointed by the Booker Prize Foundation. The judges compile a longlist of 12 or 13 books ('The Man Booker Dozen'), a shortlist of six, and from this the winner is chosen.

rubrics_metrics.name: Judging process: longlist and shortlist sizes
rubrics_metrics.description: The judges are responsible for compiling a longlist of 12 or 13 books and from this a shortlist of six books from which they then choose the winner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The longlist is sometimes called 'The Man Booker Dozen'. Judges may also call in titles (see call-in rules).

rubrics_metrics.name: Prize awards and non-divisibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Each shortlisted author receives £2,500 and a designer bound copy of his or her novel. The winning author receives a further £50,000. The prize may not be divided or withheld.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Monetary awards are fixed as above for shortlisted authors and the winner.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publishers' entry quotas
rubrics_metrics.description: Novels to be considered can only be submitted by the publishers identified in 1a. The number of novels a publisher can submit depends on that publisher’s inclusion in longlists from 2013 to 2017:
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 1 submission - publishers with no longlisting; 2 submissions - publishers with 1 or 2 longlisting(s); 3 submissions - publishers with 3 or 4 longlistings; 4 submissions - publishers with 5 or more longlistings. See the provided 2013–2017 longlists for allocation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility: original language and publication imprint
rubrics_metrics.description: Any novel in print or electronic format, written originally in English and published in the UK or Ireland by an imprint formally established in the UK or Ireland is eligible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The imprint must publish a list of at least two literary fiction novels by different authors each year. These two will not include a novel by the publisher. If the publisher is a company, the two will not include a novel by the person who owns the majority shareholding or otherwise controls the company.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility: publisher establishment criteria (UK)
rubrics_metrics.description: In determining whether the novel is published in the UK by an imprint formally established in the UK the publisher must comply with all of the following:
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The imprint sells its list in pounds sterling and where sold in print its books are distributed through national UK retail outlets; the imprint has its principal place of business in the UK and is subject to UK registration and regulation including primary liability to pay tax in the UK on all trading activities as a publisher; and the novel in question is one for which the publisher has been allocated a UK and Ireland International Standard Book Number.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility: publisher establishment criteria (Ireland)
rubrics_metrics.description: In determining whether the novel is published in Ireland by an imprint formally established in Ireland 1b. i. ii. & iii. apply but substituting Ireland for UK
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although in Ireland the publisher's list may be in euros, to remain eligible a novel must comply with 2a.iv., 2c.ii and iii., and 2d.iii. (see rules on minimum print runs, ebook availability and other publication-stage requirements).

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication date window
rubrics_metrics.description: The novel must be published in the UK or Ireland between 1 October 2017 and 30 September 2018.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If it has previously been published outside the UK and Ireland it will only be eligible if the original date of publication outside the UK and Ireland is within the previous two years, i.e. not earlier than 1 October 2015.

rubrics_metrics.name: Work form requirement: unified and substantial
rubrics_metrics.description: Every submitted novel must be a unified and substantial work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submissions of works that are fragmentary, episodic in a way that undermines unity, or insubstantial are not acceptable under this clause.

rubrics_metrics.name: Translations ineligible
rubrics_metrics.description: No English translation of a novel written originally in any other language is eligible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only works originally written in English qualify.

rubrics_metrics.name: Self-published works ineligible where author is publisher
rubrics_metrics.description: Self published novels are not eligible where the author is the publisher.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the publisher is a company specifically set up to publish the novel in question, and/or the author owns the majority shareholding or otherwise controls the company, the novel is ineligible. Novels published via a commercial arrangement through which the publisher is paid by the author are not eligible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prior prize status does not disqualify
rubrics_metrics.description: No novel is ineligible because its author has previously won either this prize or any other prize.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: As long as it otherwise complies with all the rules of the prize, any novel by an author who has previously been shortlisted for the prize may be submitted in addition to, and will not form part of, the publishers’ entry quotas.

rubrics_metrics.name: Author living requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The author of the novel must be living at the time it is submitted or called in.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The novel will only remain eligible for as long as its author is alive through the various stages of the prize up to the time of the announcement of the winner, although this is subject to the discretion of the Literary Director.

rubrics_metrics.name: Literary Director authority
rubrics_metrics.description: The decision of the Literary Director as to whether a novel is eligible shall be final and binding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No correspondence will be entered into regarding the Literary Director's eligibility determination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission deadlines and required copies (initial & final)
rubrics_metrics.description: Completed entry forms must be received by Four Colman Getty by Friday 9 March 2018. Where print or proof copies are already available eight copies together with a PDF of the text must be sent at the same time. Friday 15 June 2018 is the deadline for submitting eight copies of the finished texts, which can be final proofs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If final proofs, eight copies of the finished novel must then be received by Four Colman Getty as soon as they become available.

rubrics_metrics.name: E-book acceptance condition
rubrics_metrics.description: E-books are accepted on condition that the publisher is prepared, if necessary, to send eight bound print copies to Four Colman Getty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: E-book submissions are allowed, but the Foundation may require physical copies for judging; publishers must be prepared to supply them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimum print run requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Unless published only as an ebook, at the date of publication of the novel at least 1,000 copies must be available for retail in the UK (or in the case of a novel published in Ireland, in the UK and Ireland).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Special provisions apply if the novel is longlisted or shortlisted but not published until after announcement (see 2c.iii. and 2d.iii.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Rejection of substantially altered proofs/finished copies
rubrics_metrics.description: The Literary Director, in consultation with the chair of the judges, may reject any revised proof or finished copy which differs substantially or materially from a first submitted proof, and the novel concerned will not be further considered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publishers should ensure final copies match first-submitted proofs in substance to avoid disqualification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publisher publicity materials requirement (by June 15)
rubrics_metrics.description: By Friday 15 June 2018, in addition to the entry form, publishers must email to Four Colman Getty a high res image of the book jacket, a press release, author biog and photograph.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These materials are required for publicity and administration if the title is longlisted/shortlisted/wins.

rubrics_metrics.name: Call-in nominations: process and justification
rubrics_metrics.description: Each imprint may also provide, by Friday 9 March 2018, a list of up to five further eligible novels, accompanied by a copy or proof and a justification for each novel explaining why it should be considered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If no text is available at the time of call-in, it should be forwarded as soon as available. An imprint which only publishes one literary fiction novel a year may provide a justification for that novel as long as the novel is otherwise eligible. The justification must not exceed 250 words and must be written and signed by the author’s commissioning editor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Judges' call-in powers and selection from nominations
rubrics_metrics.description: The judges will call in no fewer than eight and no more than 12 from all such nominations they receive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The judges may also call in any novel published between 1 October 2017 and 30 September 2018, even if that novel has not been submitted or nominated; if the publisher agrees that the novel is to be considered then the publisher must sign an undertaking to comply with all rules of the prize.

rubrics_metrics.name: Longlist: publisher obligations on availability, branding and accessible copies
rubrics_metrics.description: If a novel is longlisted its publisher will: (i) where the novel was published before the announcement of the longlist and when submitted or called in was only available in print format, make the novel available for sale as an ebook within 10 days of the announcement of the longlist; (ii) where the novel was published before the announcement and when submitted or called in was published only as an ebook, have no fewer than 1,000 print copies available for retail sale in the UK (or UK and Ireland for Irish-published) within 10 days of the announcement; (iii) where the novel is published after the announcement of the longlist, then on the publication date have the minimum of 1,000 print copies available for retail sale and the novel must also be available for sale as an ebook.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publishers must use best endeavours to ensure that where print runs of the longlisted novel refer to the longlisting on the front or back cover, Man Booker Prize branding will be used; the submitting publisher must bring this to the attention of the literary agent and, where able, to counterparts elsewhere. Within 14 days of the longlist announcement provide an electronic text version to the RNIB (or other approved body) for producing accessible copies for visually impaired persons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Shortlist: publisher financial and accessibility obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: If a novel is shortlisted its publisher will: (i) contribute £5,000 towards general publicity; (ii) inform rights owners that accessible copies for the visually impaired are being produced and distributed; (iii) where the novel is published after the announcement of the shortlist, on the publication date have the minimum of 1,000 print copies available for retail sale in the UK (or UK and Ireland) and the novel must also be available for sale as an ebook.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Shortlisted publishers have a defined publicity contribution and must cooperate on accessibility and publication availability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Winner: publisher publicity contribution
rubrics_metrics.description: The publisher of the winning novel will contribute a further £5,000 towards general publicity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is in addition to the £5,000 contribution required if shortlisted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Marketing and author availability expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: It is a strict condition of entry that publishers agree to make it a priority to ensure that authors whose books are submitted or called in make themselves available for publicity and events from longlist stage on and that if shortlisted, authors will attend the award ceremony.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If there is any problem over the author’s availability, Four Colman Getty must be informed immediately. The publisher, publicist and agent of a longlisted author are strongly advised to attend a briefing meeting convened shortly after the longlist is announced. None of the print copies required as part of the submissions process or as call-ins will be returned to the publishers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality of submissions and call-ins
rubrics_metrics.description: All submissions, call-in nominations and judges’ call-ins are made on a confidential basis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publishers and agents should treat the entry and call-in process as confidential.
